a.label: a) They were both annoyed...
a.why: This explains the mutual annoyance introduced by line j) 'Was he annoyed?', so it follows at position 6.

b.label: b) Oh, what went wrong?
b.why: This reacts to line e) saying it was 'disastrous', asking what happened, so it follows at position 3.

c.label: c) Well, I'm going to carry on working...
c.why: This responds to the invitation for a drink in line h), closing the conversation at position 10.

d.label: d) How did you turn it round?
d.why: This asks how the situation was resolved, following the account of what went wrong at position 7.

e.label: e) It's fine now, but at the start of the year...
e.why: This answers the opening question f) about how the relationship is going, at position 2.

g.label: g) Well, I went over my contact's head...
g.why: This explains what went wrong, answering line b), at position 4.

h.label: h) Glad it worked out. Anyway, are you free...
h.why: This reacts positively to the resolution in line i) and changes topic to invite a drink, at position 9.

i.label: i) Well, I had to build up my relationship again...
i.why: This answers d) by explaining how the relationship was rebuilt, at position 8.

j.label: j) Was he annoyed?
j.why: This follows on from g)'s account of going over the contact's head, at position 5.

g1.label: 1. have a friendly relationship
g1.why: ‘Get on’ (well) with someone means to have a friendly relationship.

g2.label: 2. registered (at a hotel)
g2.why: ‘Check in’ means to register on arrival at a hotel.

g3.label: 3. make stronger
g3.why: ‘Build up’ (a relationship) means to make it stronger over time.

g4.label: 4. change into something successful
g4.why: ‘Turn round’ means to change a bad situation into a successful one.

g5.label: 5. postponing / delaying
g5.why: ‘Put off’ means to postpone or delay something.

g6.label: 6. appear / arrive somewhere
g6.why: ‘Turn up’ means to arrive or appear somewhere.

g8.label: 8. arrange
g8.why: ‘Set up’ means to arrange or organise something, like a meeting.

g9.label: 9. continue
g9.why: ‘Carry on’ means to continue doing something.
